html:
SMTO-MON-0006 — Monitors aren't available right now

GUID: 341c946a-fe3e-4c5a-a6f6-620f72b76dd8
Slug: monitor-service-unavailable
Domain: MON · Subsystem: mon

What happened

  • The agent tried to start, stop or check a monitor, but SMTO's monitor service wasn't connected to this task. Nothing was started or stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO only just started, wait until the startup screen reaches Ready, then ask the agent again in a new message. The monitor service is connected while SMTO starts, so an early request can find it missing.
  2. Restart SMTO (stop it, then start it again), then ask for the monitor in a new message. Restarting sets up the monitor service again for new tasks.
  3. Ask the agent to list your monitors before starting another one. This confirms the earlier request didn't create a monitor, so you don't end up with two.

What success looks like

  • The agent lists your monitors or reports that the monitor started.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO; the monitor service may have failed to start. Don't delete saved data or turn off safety checks to make monitors appear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The monitor tool (monitor.start, monitor.stop or monitor.inspect) found no monitor_manager in its execution context.

What this means

  • Start/stop/inspect capability lookup finds no monitor_manager in the execution context. Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.

Why this can happen

  • Start/stop/inspect capability lookup finds no monitor_manager in the execution context.

How to diagnose it

  • Check Controller service wiring and capability context before changing a monitor ID.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the Server initialized MonitorService (it sets services.monitor_manager and agent_runtime.monitor_manager in src/agent_runtime/api/agent_ui_support/route_groups/monitor_service.py) and that native state passes monitor_manager into the tool context. Check the Server log for monitor-service startup failures, restart the Server, then refresh the monitor list.
  • Restore the configured monitor service on the controller, then refresh the monitor list.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported runtime initialization exposes the monitor manager and current monitor inventory.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
